title: St. Lucie County property tax breaks for seniors, widows and veterans — and the March 1 deadline
seoTitle: St. Lucie County Tax Exemptions for Seniors & Vets
description: Homestead, senior, widow, disability and veteran tax exemptions in St. Lucie County: who qualifies, 2026 amounts, and how to apply by March 1, 2027.
dek: Florida gives homeowners several ways to cut the taxable value of their home, but you have to ask for them, and the deadline is March 1.
keywords: disabled veteran property tax exemption Florida
Save Our Homes portability St. Lucie
Port St. Lucie property tax exemptions

body.text: Florida does not hand out property tax breaks on its own. You have to apply. Many of the biggest breaks are for people who live in their own home, people 65 and older, widows and widowers, people with disabilities, and veterans. Some of these can save you hundreds of dollars a year. The deadline to apply for next year is March 1, 2027.
The homestead exemption is for the home you own and live in full time. It lowers the value the government can tax. In 2026 it takes up to $51,411 off your home’s taxable value.

That number has two parts. The first $25,000 counts against all property taxes, including school taxes. A second amount counts against every tax except school taxes. State law says that second part grows each year with inflation. In 2026 it is $26,411.
To qualify, you must own the home and make it your permanent home as of January 1. If you rent your home out on January 1, you can lose the exemption for that year.

body.title: Save Our Homes: the cap that grows over time
body.text: Once you have a homestead exemption, the yearly rise in your home’s assessed value is capped at 3% or the rate of inflation, whichever is less. Over many years, this cap can keep your taxable value far below what the home would sell for. If you move to a new Florida home, you can carry that savings with you. This is called portability. You can move up to $500,000 of savings, but you must set up the new homestead within three tax years of leaving the old one and apply by March 1.
Extra help for owners 65 and older

Florida lets counties and cities give an extra exemption of up to $50,000 to homeowners who are 65 or older and have low household income. The St. Lucie County Property Appraiser lists this exemption. For 2026, your household income for the year before could not be more than $38,686. The state sets a new limit each year.

This extra break only lowers the county or city taxes of a government that has chosen to offer it. It does not lower school taxes. Ask the Property Appraiser which of your taxes it would lower. To apply, you fill out an income form called the DR-501SC. Have last year’s tax return or income papers ready.
Widows, widowers and people with disabilities
State law gives a $5,000 exemption to a widow or widower. Divorced people do not qualify. If you remarry, you lose it. Bring a copy of your spouse’s death certificate to a Property Appraiser office.

The same $5,000 exemption is open to people who are blind or totally and permanently disabled. The first time, you need proof. That can be a form signed by a Florida doctor (DR-416) or a Social Security disability award letter. Some people who use a wheelchair, are legally blind, or are quadriplegic may get a full exemption. Most of these full exemptions have an income limit too.

items: Veterans with a service-connected disability of 10% or more, and an honorable discharge, can get a $5,000 exemption. A surviving spouse who has not remarried may also qualify.
Veterans with a service-connected total and permanent disability can have their homestead fully exempt. A surviving spouse who keeps the home and does not remarry can keep it.
Veterans 65 or older with a combat-related disability can get a discount on their tax equal to their disability percentage. This uses form DR-501DV.
Bring a current letter from the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs the first time you apply.

body.text: What is on the November 3 ballot

Voters will decide Amendment 3 on November 3, 2026. It needs at least 60% of the vote to pass. If it passes, the homestead exemption for non-school taxes would rise to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028. School taxes would still use the $25,000 exemption. People who are not Florida residents by December 31, 2026, would wait until their fifth year of exemption for the bigger amount.

The Pinellas County Property Appraiser says Amendment 3 would not end Save Our Homes or portability. It would not change the senior, widow, veteran or disability exemptions either. Either way, you still need to apply.

items: Check your tax bill or TRIM notice. Look for the word homestead and any other exemptions you already have.
Make a list of the exemptions you may qualify for: senior, widow or widower, disability, or veteran.
Gather papers: a Florida driver’s license, your deed, last year’s income papers, a death certificate, a doctor’s form, or a VA letter.
Apply online at paslc.gov, or go to an office. Fort Pierce: 2300 Virginia Avenue. St. Lucie West: 250 NW Country Club Drive, Port St. Lucie. You can walk in or make an appointment.
Call the St. Lucie County Property Appraiser at 772-462-1000 with questions. The exemptions page also lists 772-462-1021.
Apply by March 1, 2027. You can file early. You must own and live in the home on January 1, 2027.

body.title: Tell them when things change
body.text: If you move, rent out your home, change your mailing address, or put the house in a trust, call the Property Appraiser. A homestead does not move with you by itself. A new home or a title change needs a new application.

faq.q: When is the deadline to apply for a property tax exemption in St. Lucie County?
faq.a: March 1 of the tax year. For 2027 taxes, apply by March 1, 2027. You can file early, and you must own and live in the home on January 1.

faq.q: What was the income limit for the senior exemption in 2026?
faq.a: Household income for the prior year could not be more than $38,686. The Florida Department of Revenue sets a new limit each year.

faq.q: How much is the widow or widower exemption?
faq.a: $5,000 off your home’s taxable value under Florida law. You must be widowed on January 1 and not remarried. Divorced people do not qualify.

faq.q: Does Amendment 3 change the senior or veteran exemptions?
faq.a: The Pinellas County Property Appraiser says it does not change senior, widow, veteran or disability exemptions, Save Our Homes, or portability. It needs 60% of the vote on November 3, 2026.
